_comment: Oklahoma 2027 AHTC Application Instructions, OHFA, effective January 1, 2027. OHFA defines its QAP as these Instructions plus the Application Form and the Chapter 36 Rules; this document holds the scoring. The bundled PDF was converted from .docx, so the table of contents' page numbers do not match; page numbers here are PDF page indices. TWO SCORING SYSTEMS, recorded as tracks. The default track is the 9% Selection Criteria, pp.27-38: ten scored criteria, negative points and a tie breaker. 'state_credit' is the ranking of 4% bond applications that request Oklahoma State Tax Credits (pp.14-17): four ordered preference categories, then a 12-point efficiency score within each. NO TOTAL IS STATED for either. Hand-summed before loading: the nine self-scored criteria on the Attachment #11 score sheet (p.49-50) list 5 + 10 + 10 + 8 + 3 + 3 + 10 + 3 + 10 = 62. Because SC.5 is barred to projects taking 8 in SC.4, those two together can reach only 8, which leaves 59. Add the 24-point Development Cost Efficiency, which staff score against the round and which the sheet omits: 83. The loader matched. The 83 therefore includes 24 points no applicant can predict. One contradiction is recorded in SC.9: the body gives every amenity 1 point, while Attachment #13 gives the storm shelter or safe room 5. Thresholds are in OK_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: No total stated; the Attachment #11 'Total Self-Score' line is blank. Computed 83 = the self-scored criteria (62 flat, 59 once SC.4 and SC.5 are capped together at 8) plus 24 for Development Cost Efficiency, which is scored against the round by staff and is not on the self-score sheet. OHFA's Trustees may allocate 'irrespective of its point ranking' (p.27).

4% applications requesting State Tax Credits: ordered by four preference categories, then ranked within a category by a 12-point efficiency score (8 + 4) scored against the round. Up to $4,000,000 of State Tax Credits a year, 75% for new construction and 25% for acquisition/rehabilitation in Funding Period One.

criteria.heading: Development amenities
criteria.quote: Applicants will receive 1 Point for each Amenity selected up to 10 for a maximum of 10 Points.
criteria.note: CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved. The body says 1 point per amenity. Attachment #13 (p.53) says 'up to 10 Points (1 Point per item, except the Storm Shelter/Safe room which is 5 points)'. The maximum is 10 either way, so only the route to it differs. The attachment lists twenty-three items, from fitness centres to security systems; scattered sites score on their lowest-scoring site.

criteria.note: The largest criterion, and absent from the Attachment #11 self-score sheet because staff calculate it after the deadline: each factor is percentile-ranked against the round, so a 95th-percentile result earns 7.6 of 8 (the document's own example). An applicant cannot know this score before applying. An unfavourable change at final application bars the principals from two funding periods.

criteria.heading: Negative points
criteria.note: Posted about 30 days before the deadline and counted in the next funding period: 2 points per late report beyond three, 3 for late fee payment, 5 for an uncorrected 8823 or OHFA notice of noncompliance. The points follow common general partners, managing members and principals, and stay with a transferred development for six months.

criteria.note: Ranks 4% applications within each preference category. The factors are named for State Tax Credits, but the definitions paragraph says '"Credit" means the Federal Affordable Housing Tax Credits requested' - a definitional inconsistency recorded for the reviewer. State Tax Credits require 20% of units at or below 50% AMI and are capped at $2,000,000 per developer group a year.
